robustness: native-kernels/x86_64/pqk_x86_common.h:131-145,294-347 — callee-saved registers are pushed and popped from a single #define SAVED list so the push and pop sequences cannot drift. VRET (vzeroupper) is used on every SIMD return, there is no red zone, and the 7th argument is read via ARG7(npush). The OP_CHECK unsigned compare rejects negative ops before any memory access (161-168)

native-kernels/x86_64/pqk_x86_common.h:210-223,377-390 — lvp loads exactly ceil(len/8) validity bytes and STORE_BITS_TAIL writes exactly ceil(len/8) output bytes. The AVX2 file deliberately avoids vpmaskmov for tails (pqk_x86_avx2.S:23-25), and the AVX-512 file uses fault-suppressing {k}{z} masked loads (pqk_x86_avx512.S:620,665)

native-kernels/x86_64/pqk_x86_avx2.S:1722-1835 — the group_sum local-table path probes the stack page by page, aligns the table, restores rsp from rbp on both exits, and commits only under a proven no-wrap bound (n*max|x| < 2^62 and |sums[g]| < 2^62); otherwise it falls back to the exact path, so the overflow flag is preserved. Exact 128/192-bit overflow detection: pqk_x86_scalar.S:804-811,900 (JNE_SEXT)

native-kernels/x86_64/pqk_x86_scalar.S:1098, pqk_x86_avx2.S:2515, pqk_x86_avx512.S:1550 — .note.GNU-stack in every object. native-kernels/x86_64/pqk_x86_simd.h:16-25 and verify/run.sh:15-19 — chunk sizes can be overridden with -D, so the rare chunk-fold paths of the exact sums run in tests. verify/structure_check.py:6-23 checks the Clobbers: header lists against the disassembly, the single definition of each block, the label scheme and the skeleton tags. Weakness: the test C is written as dense one-liners (abi_check.c:14-19), and run.sh uses only 'set -e'

top_strengths: Strong shared-building-block design: every macro, table and helper is defined once in layered headers, enforced by structure_check.py, while each variant object stays self-contained

Careful memory safety: exact-byte validity loads and stores, no masked-load fault ambiguity on AVX2, fault-suppressing masks on AVX-512, and bounded prefetch look-ahead, all checked by guard-page tests
Exactness by construction: biased lane sums folded into 128/192-bit totals give precise overflow detection, and group_sum's fast path is gated by a proven no-wrap bound

Thorough verification tooling: guard pages, an ABI trampoline that checks callee-saved registers and vzeroupper state, clobber lists checked against the disassembly, chunk-size overrides, and machine-code diffing for refactors
Consistent, informative header comments stating registers, clobbers, algorithm and tail strategy, with measured rationale for performance decisions
top_weaknesses: The AVX2 variant is heavily micro-optimized for Zen 5 (rorx nibble indexing, Harley-Seal CSA trees, hybrid vector/scalar hashing, quick-reject backoff), so kernels are long (group_sum_i64 is about 250 lines) and hard to modify safely
The README is 1451 lines and partly stale: module-map line counts predate the AVX2 optimization (avx2.S 1718 vs 2515 actual, avx2.h 632 vs 932)
The Makefile does not track .h dependencies (documented at README.md:59-61), so header edits can silently leave stale objects
Verification C sources are dense one-liners and run.sh uses only 'set -e', which hurts maintainability of the test tooling
